subtopics.title: Direct and Indirect — the First Sorting

questions.question: The first sorting question of cost accounting is:
options: Can this cost be traced to ONE SPECIFIC unit? Traceable — direct; serving production in general — indirect, gathered as overheads
Is this cost large or small?
Was this cost paid in cash or on credit?
Does this cost repeat every month?

questions.question: In Lerato's Woodcraft, the timber at R60 per stool is:
options: Direct material — it becomes part of the product and is traceable to each stool

questions.question: The foreman who oversees the whole floor is:
options: Indirect labour — his wage serves every stool equally and no stool specifically, so it joins factory overheads

questions.question: The sales assistant at the counter and the showroom's rent are:
options: Not production costs at all — cost accounting fences the workshop and counts only inside the fence

subtopics.title: Prime Cost, Overheads and the Cost of One Stool

questions.question: The month's prime cost is:
options: R27 000 — direct materials R18 000 (300 × R60) plus direct labour R9 000 (300 × R30)

questions.question: Total cost of production is:
options: Prime cost R27 000 plus factory overheads R8 400 — R35 400

questions.question: The unit cost of one stool is:
options: R118 — total cost of production R35 400 divided by 300 units, the floor beneath every price

questions.question: Work-in-progress at month-end is:
options: Half-assembled units — no longer raw material, not yet finished goods — whose cost stays in the workshop until completion

subtopics.title: Fixed and Variable — the Second Sorting

questions.question: Variable costs behave so that:
options: The TOTAL moves in step with output while the PER-UNIT amount stands still — every stool carries its own R90
The per-unit amount rises with output

questions.question: Fixed costs behave so that:
options: They scale rand for rand with output
The TOTAL stands still within the month while the PER-UNIT amount falls as output rises — the same R8 400 spread wider

questions.question: At four hundred stools the unit cost becomes:
options: R111 — variable R90 plus fixed spread of R21 (8 400 over 400); making more made each stool cheaper

questions.question: A quiet month of 150 stools warns that:
options: Fixed cost per unit climbs to R56, unit cost to R146 — and the R150 price suddenly clears almost nothing

questions.question: In classification questions, every cost wears BOTH labels, meaning:
options: Its attachment (direct/indirect) AND its behaviour (fixed/variable) — timber is direct and variable; rent is overhead and fixed

questions.question: The cost statement's layers run:
options: Direct materials plus direct labour — prime cost; plus factory overheads — total cost of production; over units — unit cost
Any order, as long as the total agrees

questions.question: The classic what-if error the marker hunts is:
options: Scaling the FIXED costs with volume — stretching the rent because output rose, against the very definition of fixed
Keeping the variable cost per unit constant

questions.question: The four-move decision comment is:
options: State the figure, judge it, explain the cause, recommend the action — e.g. thin margin, risky, fixed-cost spread, build volume or trim overheads

questions.question: In Mrs Pillay's kitchen, the pastry and filling are:
options: Direct material — she can say to the cent what each samoosa carries

questions.question: The gas bottle, the pot wear and the cousin watching the frying are:
options: The overheads — real costs of keeping the kitchen cooking, traceable to no single samoosa

questions.question: The taxi fare to deliver the order is:
options: Not a making cost at all — the kitchen fence stops at the kitchen door; selling and delivering live outside it

questions.question: The order's prime cost is:
options: R2 000 — R4 of direct cost per samoosa (pastry and filling R2,50 plus frying R1,50) times 500

questions.question: The unit cost of one samoosa is:
options: R5,50 — total cost R2 750 (prime 2 000 plus overheads 750) divided by 500

questions.question: Selling at R8 each, the whole order clears:
Matching a rival's R5 price would mean:
options: Nothing — price and cost are unrelated
A fifty-cent loss on every samoosa — trade that FEELS like business while it quietly eats her savings

subtopics.title: The Rent Doesn't Care How Busy You Are

questions.question: "Some costs scale and some stand still" means:
options: Variables move rand for rand with the work while standing costs must be fed regardless of volume
Standing costs vanish in quiet months
Variable costs never change in total

questions.question: At 750 samoosas, the R750 of standing costs lands at:
options: R1 per unit — unit cost R5; busyness itself made every unit cheaper

questions.question: The slow-month warning at 150 units is:
options: The standing costs shrink to match
Standing costs land R5 on each unit — unit cost R9, ABOVE the R8 price, so every sale now loses money

questions.question: "The rent doesn't care how busy you are" teaches that:
options: Quiet months are cheaper to run
Standing costs are a drumbeat — match your volume to it, or it plays you out of business
